title: GPU OOM & CUDA/driver mismatch debug notes — Olivia Mendes
content:
Summary:
Quick scratchpad documenting recent GPU OOM and CUDA / driver mismatch errors seen on a couple of Dedicated nodes (p4d/rt-prod pool). Goal is to capture commands tried, error snippets, environment, hypotheses, and next steps for handoff to SRE if needed.

Context / Symptoms:
- Intermittent OOMs during model warmup + quantized attention tests (Llama2-13B-quant).
- Failures sometimes show as pure CUDA OOM, other times show 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version' or libcudart mismatch when launching docker container.
- Affected instances: rt-prod-pool-3 (p4d.24xlarge variants), observed across a few deployments after kernel/driver roll.

Environment snapshot (collected):
- nvidia-smi (host):
  +-------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.11    Driver Version: 535.54.11 |
  +-------------------------------------------------+
- docker image: redwood/serving-runtime:2025-01-10-gpu
- CUDA inside container: nvcc --version -> Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.105
- pytorch built with CUDA: torch.version.cuda -> '12.1'
- CUDA toolkit libs inside container: /usr/local/cuda/lib64 -> libcudart.so.12.1

Observed errors (log snippets):
1) OOM during kv-cache allocation on first prompt:
   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 10.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 20.10 GiB already allocated; 2.50 GiB free; 20.80 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
   (Triggered by model.forward() on warmup batch)

2) Driver/runtime mismatch seen when container started after host driver update: 
   [W CudaIPCTypes.cpp:127] Warning: CUDA IPC is enabled, but the NVIDIA driver on the host is older than the CUDA runtime in the container. This may cause failures.
   CUDART_VERSION mismatch: Host driver 535.54.11 < container runtime 12010 -> libcudart mismatch

3) Intermittent segfault in python when using torch.distributed with NCCL:
   Fatal error in MPI_Init: Other MPI error, error stack: ...
   Aborted (core dumped)

Commands/traces I ran:
- Host driver check:
  $ nvidia-smi -q | head -n 20
- Container check (run with --gpus all):
  $ docker run --gpus all -it --rm redwood/serving-runtime:2025-01-10-gpu bash -c "python -c "import torch,sys;print(torch.cuda.is_available());print(torch.version.cuda);print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))""
- Verified libcudart in container:
  $ ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart*
- Looked at dmesg for GPU errors: dmesg | egrep -i "nvrm|nvidia|gpu|oom"
- PyTorch memory snapshot script run at failure time (attached to ticket):
  $ python tools/trace_allocs.py --pid <pid> --out /tmp/allocs.json

What I tried / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Driver on the host is newer but incompatible with container's runtime or vice versa. Some nodes were updated mid-roll and have driver/runtime misalignment.
  Action: Reboot hosts after driver updates; make sure container CUDA runtime <= host driver compatibility matrix.
- Hypothesis B: PyTorch caching + reserved memory accounts for big chunk of reserved memory; combined with model quantization memory spikes leads to OOM.
  Action: Set TORCH_CACHE_SIZE or disable caching; call torch.cuda.empty_cache() in warmup path; try max_split_size_mb; test with environment var PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
- Hypothesis C: NCCL + mixed libcudnn / cudart versions cause segfaults in distributed path.
  Action: Force NCCL version packaged in image, or use container built against host's driver (multi-version image).

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Rolled back to older container built with CUDA 11.8 for a subset of nodes -> fewer runtime mismatch logs, but slightly higher per-token latency.
- Forced container start flag: --runtime=nvidia (legacy) on one host to validate GPU access path.
- Added init script that checks nvidia-smi + nvcc and fails fast if mismatch detected; writing alert to /var/log/gpu-init-check.log
- Forcing environment: export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 to reduce fragmentation during warmup. Reduced OOM frequency but not eliminated.

Data / reproducibility notes:
- Can reproduce OOM with the following minimal workload on affected node (runs in ~20s):
  python - <<'PY'
  import torch, time
  model = torch.nn.Transformer(encoder_layers=12, d_model=2048).cuda()
  inp = torch.randint(0,1000,(16,1024)).cuda()
  for _ in range(3):
      out = model(inp)
      time.sleep(0.2)
  PY
- The mismatch message shows up reliably when container cuda version > host driver supported runtime.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Collect driver/kernel/package versions across all rt-prod nodes and map against container CUDA versions. Script: inventory-drivers.sh (attach output to JIRA-ENGINE-1276).
- [ ] Create a small smoke-test that runs at container start: verify torch.cuda.get_device_properties + lat/throughput microtest. Fail if mismatch.
- [ ] Add automated alert when dmesg contains NVRM messages during rolling updates.
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to pin driver versions during a rollout and schedule a maintenance window to upgrade containers after drivers are stable.
- [ ] Try building a multi-CUDA-toolkit image (compat 11.x and 12.x libraries) or switch to runtime-host-matching build.

Notes for SRE handoff:
- Likely causes: mid-roll host driver update + container images built against newer CUDA runtime.
- Symptoms vary: sometimes pure OOM (memory), sometimes runtime mismatch warnings causing GPU failures.
- Priority: medium-high (affects warmup reliability and model rollouts).

Raw snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- nvidia-smi summary: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name,memory.total --format=csv
- container cuda: docker run --gpus all --rm redwood/serving-runtime:2025-01-10-gpu bash -c "printf '%s
' $(nvcc --version) $(python -c 'import torch;print(torch.version.cuda)')"

If handing off: attach the alloc trace (/tmp/allocs.json), dmesg dump, and inventory csv.

Notes to self: prioritize reproducible small repro for SRE. Save log excerpts to Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-RT-3912) and link to JIRA ticket JIRA-ENGINE-1276.

End of notes.
